deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann's 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (Göttingen, c. 1853). In it a space-filling 'Stoff' (aether) transmits gravitation, light and heat. On the previous page he labels a material particle at O by Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) at time t, and the same particle at another time t' by (x',y',z') = functions of (x,y,z).

(1) Strain. With F = ∂(x',y',z')/∂(x,y,z), the squared length element at t' is ds'^2 = dx^T C dx, where C = F^T F is symmetric positive definite. This is a homogeneous quadratic form in dx, dy, dz.

(2) Principal-axis theorem. There is an orthogonal matrix R with rows (α_i, β_i, γ_i). Set ds_i = α_i dx + β_i dy + γ_i dz. Then:
- ds^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 = Σ ds_i^2;
- ds'^2 = Σ G_i^2 ds_i^2.
Here the G_i^2 are the eigenvalues of C, so the G_i are the principal stretches (singular values of F). Riemann defines the principal dilatations λ_i = G_i − 1.

(3) Constitutive hypotheses.
- The difference between the particle's earlier forms and its form at time t produces a force tending to change the present form.
- The influence of an earlier form fades with its age and becomes negligible beyond some time.
- Only forms with small dilatations matter, so the λ_i may be treated as infinitesimal.
- Hence the restoring forces f_i are linear in λ.
- Isotropy ('Gleichartigkeit') requires f_1 to be symmetric under λ_2↔λ_3, with f_2 and f_3 obtained by permutation. So f_1 = aλ_1 + b(λ_2+λ_3), and cyclically.
- The total virtual moment (virtual work) is Σ δλ_i f_i.
- Relabelling constants (a_new = b, b_new = a − b), f_i = a(λ_1+λ_2+λ_3) + bλ_i.
- Then Σ δλ_i f_i = ½ δ[a(Σλ)^2 + b Σλ^2]. This is the isotropic quadratic strain energy, the Lamé form with a ~ λ_Lamé and b ~ 2μ.

(4) Splitting into volume and line-element parts.
- To first order, the relative volume change is dV'/dV − 1 = G_1G_2G_3 − 1 ≈ Σλ_i. [linearisation mine]
- For a line element with direction cosines n_i, (ds'−ds)/ds = sqrt(Σ G_i^2 n_i^2) − 1 ≈ Σ λ_i n_i^2. [mine]
- Averaging the square of the latter over directions gives (2Σλ^2 + (Σλ)^2)/15. [mine] So a volume term plus a line-element term spans the same two-parameter family of energies.
- Riemann therefore states the law: the force tending to lengthen ds, produced by the difference of states at t and t', is a (dV'−dV)/dV + b (ds'−ds)/ds.
- He interprets the first part as resistance to volume change without change of form, and the second as resistance of a physical line element to change of length.

(5) Memory. There is no reason the two effects should decay with time in the same way. Superposing the effects of all earlier forms, the 'force' on (or rate δds/dt of) the line element at time t is
∫_{-∞}^t (dV'−dV)/dV ψ(t−t') dt' + ∫_{-∞}^t (ds'−ds)/ds φ(t−t') dt'.
This is a linear hereditary (viscoelastic) law with separate bulk and line-element memory kernels ψ and φ. It generalises the one-dimensional kernel equation y_t = α^2 ∫^t y_xx φ(t−τ) dτ on the previous page. The next page asks what ψ and φ must be for gravitation (volume part) and light and heat (line-element part) to be transmitted.
errors: 'stets und nur auf Eine Weise': the orthonormal ds_i are unique only up to order and sign. They are not unique at all when two eigenvalues G_i^2 coincide (any orthonormal basis of the eigenspace works).

Interpreting a(dV'−dV)/dV as resistance to 'volume change without change of form' is loose. The line-element term b(ds'−ds)/ds also contributes to the volume (trace) part, since its directional average gives (Σλ)^2 as well as Σλ^2. The split is a reparametrisation of the two isotropic constants, not an orthogonal bulk/deviatoric decomposition. The constants silently change meaning again.

In the final formula it is ambiguous whether the integral is a force or the rate δds/dt itself; the phrase 'die Kraft von δds/dt' is unclear. With the first-order (inertia-free) dynamics of the previous page, the integral seems meant to equal the rate. Dimensionally, the kernels must absorb the constants a and b.

The directions of 'Übergang von der ersteren Form zur letzteren' and the sign convention (t' earlier than t) are left implicit. The convention is consistent if t' < t: if ds' > ds, the force lengthens ds.
No dynamical check is given that the variation form is conservative. It is, automatically, because the coefficient matrix is symmetric.

results.what: Reduction of the deformation metric ds'^2 to principal axes: ds'^2 = Σ G_i^2 ds_i^2 with ds^2 = Σ ds_i^2; principal dilatations λ_i = G_i − 1
results.modern_name: Principal stretches / spectral decomposition of the right Cauchy–Green tensor (singular values of the deformation gradient)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (1827–1841, principal strains); principal-axis theorem from Cauchy/Jacobi

results.what: Isotropic linear restoring forces from permutation symmetry, giving energy ½[a(Σλ)^2 + bΣλ^2]
results.modern_name: Isotropic linear elastic strain energy (two Lamé constants)

results.what: Writing the isotropic law as volume-change resistance plus line-element length-change resistance
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy/Lamé; Green; Stokes (1845, bulk vs shear)

results.what: Hereditary law: present force/rate equals a time integral over past strains, with separate memory kernels ψ (volume) and φ (line element)
results.modern_name: Linear viscoelasticity with memory (Boltzmann superposition, hereditary integrals); separate bulk and shear relaxation functions
results.usually_credited_to: Boltzmann (1874); cf. Maxwell (1867), later Volterra (hereditary mechanics, 1909–1913)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of the 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' fragment. It was published by Dedekind and Weber in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) and is often discussed: Riemann's aether with memory kernels ψ and φ anticipating hereditary viscoelasticity. The elasticity content is standard Cauchy–Lamé theory. The memory-integral idea predates Boltzmann (1874), but it is already known in the literature as Riemann's.

'wegen der Gleichartigkeit [?] des Aethers [?]' is uncertain in the image; the sense (isotropy/homogeneity of the medium) is clear from the symmetry argument.

'so wird die Kraft von [?] δds/dt' is unclear; possibly 'die Änderung δds/dt' or 'die Kraft oder δds/dt'. The integral formula itself (∫_{-∞}^t … ψ(t−t')dt' + ∫_{-∞}^t … φ(t−t')dt') matches the image.
